follow100Note: Of every $100 of revenue, $86.35 came from Premium and $13.65 from ads. Direct costs took $73.30 and running costs $28.74, finance items cost $1.53 and tax was a $1.66 benefit, leaving a $1.91 loss. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Spotify reports in euros under IFRS. Dollar figures are converted at €1 = $1.1050 (ECB euro reference rate at Dec 29, 2023). As reported: revenue €3,671M · gross profit €980M · operating loss €75M · net loss €70M.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: vs a year ago (+20% constant currency)

oneTimers: Operating expenses included €143M of charges from efficiency actions taken late in the quarter — €110M of employee severance and related charges from the December workforce reduction plus a €33M impairment charge on real estate assets. Excluding them, adjusted operating income was €68M, more than double Q3 2023's €32M.
Operating expenses included €33M of 'social charges' — Swedish payroll taxes on share-based pay that swing with Spotify's share price — versus €1M a year ago.
Gross profit carried €4M of net severance related charges, and the quarter's €143M in efficiency charges included €4M in cost of revenue.
The quarter carried a €61M income tax benefit on a €131M pre-tax loss, versus a €21M benefit a year ago.
otherDetail: Finance items netted -€56M — €46M of finance income against €102M of finance costs. A year ago finance items netted -€60M.

segments.name: Premium
segments.note: Subscriptions — 236 million people paying monthly, up 15% YoY; revenue per user (ARPU) €4.60, up 1% (+5% in constant currency) as price rises outweighed product mix; gross margin 29.1%.

segments.name: Ad-Supported
segments.note: The free tier's advertising business — revenue grew 12% (17% in constant currency) on growth across all regions, with music ads up double digits and podcast ads up in the healthy double-digit range; its gross margin rose to 11.6%.

takeaways.text: Monthly active users grew 23% to 602 million — 28 million net additions in the quarter, the second largest Q4 in Spotify's history — contributing to record full-year net additions of 113 million. Premium subscribers rose 15% to 236 million, with record full-year net additions of 31 million, and ad-supported users grew 28% to 379 million.
takeaways.title: Record user growth

takeaways.text: The reported operating loss of €75M narrowed from €231M a year ago, but it included €143M of efficiency charges — severance from the December workforce reduction and real estate impairments. Excluding them, adjusted operating income was €68M, more than double Q3 2023. Gross margin hit 26.7%, up 140 bps YoY, on better music and podcast profitability.
takeaways.title: Profitable underneath the charges

takeaways.text: Free cash flow was €396M, bringing trailing-12-month free cash flow to €678M and the cash pile to €4.3B. Net loss narrowed to €70M from €270M a year ago. Guidance for Q1 2024: 618M users, 239M subscribers, €3.6B revenue, 26.4% gross margin and €180M operating income.
takeaways.title: Cash piled up

verdict: Spotify grew revenue 16% to €3.67B (about $4.1B) and narrowed its operating loss to €75M as 602 million monthly users and 236 million paying subscribers each grew double digits — but €143M of efficiency charges kept the quarter in the red, with a net loss of €70M.
